title: Ukrainian LSU women's basketball player leaves team over signing of Russian recruit
text:
Kate Koval departed the program “to remain true to myself, my values and my country.”
Ukrainian forward Kate Koval revealed she left LSU because the Tigers signed a Russian player, adding that remaining "true to myself, my values" and finding another team were her only option.
“The timing of this situation and the deeply personal effect it has had on me, my family and those we care about who continue to live through and fight this war ultimately made me question whether LSU remained the right place for me,”. “This decision has not been easy. While I understand and respect that roster decisions are a part of college basketball, I have to remain true to myself, my values and my country.
”It was widely believed that Koval, 20, opted out in opposition to LSU’s signing 6-foot-5 Russian center Anna Minaeva, who previously played Koval said Wednesday that she’s proud of her father’s service in the Ukrainian military as it defends the nation against Russia’s 4½-year-long LSU coach Kim Mulkey announced last week that Koval was leaving the program for “personal reasons” after just one season in Baton Rouge.
“My father serves in the Ukrainian military and takes tremendous pride in defending his country against Russian aggression,” Koval wrote in a statement. “For me, this war is not distant or abstract. People close to me have been killed and wounded in Russian attacks, and places where I grew up and first began playing basketball have been destroyed by missile strikes.
” Koval said that she enjoyed her time in Baton Rouge but that the Russian player’s addition to the LSU roster made the setting untenable.
“I hope the NCAA recognizes the circumstances surrounding my situation and understands the seriousness and deep nature of this matter,” she said. “More than anything, I hope I am given the opportunity to compete at another school during the upcoming 2026-27 basketball season. ”.
